name: Sovereign debt stress
summary: France–Bund spread 152.9bp on 9 Nov, just above the 150bp Alert line and below its 174.6bp peak of 22 Oct
state: France's 10-year yield was 4.79% on 9 Nov against 3.26% on the Bund, a spread of 152.9bp, above the 150bp Alert line; it was 161.8bp on 3 Nov and peaked at 174.6bp on 22 Oct (Banque de France and Bundesbank data via Ideal Investisseur). The OAT yield fell to about 4.70% on 10 Nov, a six-week low, as oil prices eased (Trading Economics). No failed G7 auction or emergency ECB buying was found as of 10 Nov.
for_you: Higher French borrowing costs can spread to other European bond markets and affect funds holding government debt. A move back below 150bp would lower this to Watch.

sources.title: Ideal Investisseur — OAT/Bund spread today: 152.9 bps as of 9 Nov 2026
Trading Economics — France 10-year bond yield hits six-week low

why: When big governments struggle to borrow, it raises everyone's costs and can force sudden austerity or money-printing.
drivers: Deficits, auction demand, ratings actions, political shocks, long-end yields.

rubric.alert: Failed G7 auction, emergency central-bank purchases, France–Bund > 150bp, or Italy–Bund > 250bp.
rubric.watch: G7 30-year yields at multi-decade highs, a G7 downgrade, or France–Bund 80–150bp / Italy–Bund 150–250bp.
rubric.normal: Auctions orderly; France–Bund spread < 80bp; Italy–Bund < 150bp; no G7 downgrades this month.
